analysis: Examined GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift (base vs head) and its test patch. Changes: (1) RawControls.capture now parses a GLM-style `thinking` object, nullable OpenRouter fields, and summary levels; unknown `reasoning` members, bad `thinking` types and `preserve_thinking` (even null) remain `invalid`. `exclude:true` and `include_reasoning:false` still hit excludesReasoning. Contradictory on/off spellings are still refused in validate() and additionalContext. (2) Returned assistant reasoning (`reasoning` / `reasoning_details` text entries) is captured with a separate best-effort `try?` pass over `messages` and replayed as `reasoning_content` (head lines 352-362, 397-406). It applies only to assistant turns without an existing reasoningContent, and only when the capture count equals request.messages.count with offset 0...1. Otherwise it is dropped. This is consumer-controlled text with the same trust as the existing reasoning_content field. It enters only the prompt for the consumer's own request and adds no new cross-tenant or provider-to-consumer channel. Test lines 645+ show clear_thinking still drops it. (3) Empty tool-call arguments now map to `{}` (line 443). The delimiter and unique-ID checks still run on non-empty arguments. (4) The rejection of `strict` tools (base 266-268) is removed. The head comment says every auto call is validated against its declared schema via ToolConstraintValidation.validate before exposure. That code is not in the supplied evidence and is a contract for the next pass to confirm. It is not a provider-side secrecy or attestation control. Residual: the messages array is decoded twice (extra CPU/memory bounded by upstream request-size limits, not visible here). No change touches keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, the coordinator wire contract, cache storage or fan control (A-001..A-017, T-041 unaffected). No regression identified.
